title: 18.1 million people face acute food insecurity as prices climb
excerpt: The IPC projection for September to December is up from 15.3 million in the lean season. Bread, milk and hundreds of medicines now cost more.
content:
About 18.1 million people in Bangladesh are projected to face acute food insecurity between September and December 2026, including about 787,000 at emergency level, according to the Integrated Food Security Phase Classification (IPC) figures cited by The Business Standard on Thursday (19 November).

From May to August, 15.3 million people, 15% of the population analysed, faced acute food insecurity, the IPC found.

Prices and poverty

The Bangladesh Bread, Biscuit and Confectionery Manufacturers Association raised prices by 20% in late October; its president, Jalal Uddin, said production costs had risen at least 30% in six months. Milk has risen from Tk 100 to Tk 110 to 115 a litre. A comparison of manufacturers' price lists by the paper found prices of hundreds of medicines up 5% to 10% in three months. AZM Zakir Hossain, secretary of the Bangladesh Association of Pharmaceutical Industries, said production costs had risen at least 30%.

The Policy Research Institute's State of the Real Economy 2026 report put poverty at 27.9% in 2025, with another 18% vulnerable to falling into it. Zahid Hussain, former lead economist at the World Bank's Dhaka office, said incomes had not kept up with costs.

Why it matters

The rise from 15.3 million to 18.1 million people means food assistance, nutrition and cash programmes may face more demand going into winter, while higher medicine prices add to the cost of illness for poor households.

What to watch

Government open market sales and food-friendly programme coverage, the next IPC update, and medicine price controls.

Sources

  • The Business Standard: Food, medicine: rising costs squeeze families, 19 November 2026
